column3: Nehemiah, cupbearer to King Artaxerxes, asks about the Jews who returned to Jerusalem.
He prays to the God of the heavens, then asks the king to send him to rebuild the city of his forefathers. The king grants it.
Telling no one, he rides out in the dark and inspects the broken walls and the burned gates.
He tells the people how the hand of his God has been with him.
Sanballat the Horonite hears that the wall is going up. He is furious, and he mocks the Jews before his army.
The work goes on. The wall is joined together up to half its height, for the people have a heart to work.
The enemies plot together to come and fight against Jerusalem and throw it into confusion.
The plot is no secret now. The builders answer it with prayer, and with a guard on the wall by day and by night.
Half the men work, half hold the spears. The builders carry the loads with one hand and a weapon in the other. Where the horn sounds, gather.
The work has drawn the people from their fields. Hungry, in debt to their own brothers, some families are giving up their children as servants for grain. Nehemiah is very angry.
He puts it to the nobles and the rulers: stop the interest, and give back the fields, the vineyards, the olive groves and the houses. They agree, and the people praise Yahweh.
He never takes the governor’s food allowance. A hundred and fifty men eat at his table at his own cost, and he works on the wall with them. Today the valley is quiet.
The Tekoites repair a second stretch of the wall. Their nobles would not put their necks to the work; the rest of the Tekoites more than make up for it.
Four times they send the same invitation, meaning to harm him. Four times he gives the same answer.
A fifth time he sends, this time with an open letter in his hand: a rumour that Nehemiah means to be king, and that it will be reported to the king.
A man shut in at home warns that they will come by night to kill Nehemiah: meet in the temple and shut its doors. It is a trap. He was hired to make Nehemiah afraid.
The last stone is set and the doors hang in their gates. From the Sheep Gate all the way around, the wall stands.
The enemies hear of it, and all the nations around are afraid. Their schemes have come to nothing.
Two great choirs of thanksgiving go in procession on top of the wall, one to the right and one to the left, and meet at the house of God.
Eliashib the high priest and his brothers the priests take up the work at the Sheep Gate.
The sons of Hassenaah build the Fish Gate and lay its beams.
Joiada and Meshullam repair the Gate of the Old City. Its stone lies in the burned rubble.
Goldsmiths and ointment makers (craftsmen, not masons) repair the wall as far as the Broad Wall.
Malchijah and Hasshub repair another section, and the Tower of the Bake Ovens.
Hanun and the people of Zanoah rebuild the Valley Gate and a thousand cubits of wall.
Malchijah son of Rechab repairs the Gate of the Ash Heaps, far from where the stone is stacked.
Shallun repairs the Fountain Gate, down by the pool at the King's Garden.
The temple servants living on Ophel work as far as the Water Gate. Guards keep watch by night.
Above the Horse Gate the priests each repair in front of their own house.
Shemaiah, the keeper of the East Gate, makes repairs.
The last stretch: from the Inspection Gate back around to the Sheep Gate. Close the circuit.
